questions.q: What is 'automated scanning,' per this lesson?
options: A catalog tool connecting directly to source systems to pull technical metadata automatically, on a schedule
A human manually typing in every table's definition one at a time
A one-time process that can never be repeated
A method for deleting outdated glossary terms
questions.explain: Automated scanning is the same INFORMATION_SCHEMA-style extraction from Lesson 12, run automatically against source systems rather than by hand.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say a catalog built on scanning alone is 'technically comprehensive and completely useless for business users'?
options: It can report structural facts like data type, but not business meaning, ownership, or context
Because scanning always produces incorrect data types
Because scanning is illegal under most data protection regulations
Because scanned tables cannot be searched at all
questions.explain: A scan can tell you CustomerId is an INT, but not that it's the key every revenue report joins on or who to ask when it looks wrong — that's manual curation's job.

questions.q: What goes wrong in a catalog that relies on manual curation alone, per this lesson?
options: It ends up with silent gaps nobody notices, since nothing flags an undocumented table as missing
It becomes too expensive to maintain within one week
It automatically deletes all previously curated entries
It can only store exactly one table at a time
questions.explain: Curation-only catalogs are accurate where someone wrote something, but an undocumented table simply doesn't appear — there's no automatic signal that something is missing.

questions.q: In the worked OrderTotal example, which fields came from automated scanning versus manual curation?
options: Data type and row count came from scanning; the business definition and glossary link came from curation
All fields came exclusively from automated scanning
All fields came exclusively from manual curation
The owner field came from scanning, and the data type came from curation
questions.explain: Structural facts (type, row count, last modified) are scanned automatically; business definition, glossary link, and owner require a human steward to write them.

questions.q: Per this lesson, do automated scanning and manual curation compete with each other, or complement each other?
options: They complement each other — scanning guarantees coverage, curation supplies meaning, and neither substitutes for the other
They compete directly, and an organization should pick only one
Scanning always makes curation completely unnecessary
Curation always makes scanning completely unnecessary
questions.explain: A mature catalog program deliberately uses both, since each solves a different problem the other cannot.
